title: Auth header normalization induced 429 reconciliation runaway
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Summary: A regional 429 surge occurred after a routine auth rollout. The immediate cause was an unexpected interaction between header normalization in the ingress proxy and the quota key derivation code, which produced duplicate quota keys for distinct tokens in a subset of microservices. This led to quota misattribution and a cascading reconciliation job that amplified requests and caused widespread 429s across two regions for ~42 minutes. This ticket captures the incident follow-ups, root cause, and tracked action items.
impact_summary: Approx 18% of requests to the hosted API received downstream 429s at peak. ~110k requests failed across NA-West and EU-Central over a 42-minute window. Customer-facing latency increased by ~220ms due to retries. Two enterprise customers saw sustained degraded throughput and opened support tickets.
timeline_summary: 2026-03-01T10:07Z - Pager alert (error rate+429 spike); 2026-03-01T10:12Z - SRE triage: region-scoped surge, begin mitigation; 2026-03-01T10:20Z - Mitigation 1: throttling reconciliation job and pausing delayed token reconciliation; 2026-03-01T10:34Z - Mitigation 2: revert header normalization rollout in ingress and pin gateway config; 2026-03-01T10:49Z - Traffic returns to baseline; monitoring until 11:15Z; 2026-03-01T11:30Z - Post-incident meeting with PM/Design/Eng
root_cause: Two changes combined: (1) a header normalization patch in the ingress proxy that lowercased and deduped X-Auth-Token variants, and (2) a quota-key hashing change that assumed token uniqueness after trimming. In edge cases where tokens were presented in different header varieties (X-Auth-Token vs x-auth-token vs X-Forwarded-Auth), the normalized value lost a distinguishing prefix used by the quota system (org-scoped prefix). The quota enforcer calculated identical keys for distinct clients, causing credit stealing and triggering the reconciliation process. Reconciliation logic retried ownership correction by issuing synthetic attribution requests which flared into additional load and 429s (a feedback loop).
mitigations_taken: 1) Rolled back ingress header normalization rollout to previous behavior (10:34Z). 2) Disabled automatic reconciliation retries and switched to linear backoff queueing (10:20Z). 3) Applied a hotfix to quota-key derivation to preserve org prefixes when present (10:50Z). 4) Throttled reconciliation worker concurrency and added a circuit-breaker in front of the enforcer (11:00Z).
action_items: AI-1: Add a non-destructive compatibility test for header normalization + quota-key derivation (owner: Miguel Santos, estimate: 3)
AI-2: Implement reconciliation rate limits and exponential backoff with jitter; ensure workers report backpressure metrics (owner: Priya Khandelwal, estimate: 5)
AI-3: Add dedupe-safe token canonicalization tests in unit/integration suites and include org-prefix-preservation assertions (owner: Keiko Tanaka, estimate: 3)
AI-4: Deploy a structured observability panel that correlates header variants -> quota key collisions -> reconciliation events (owner: SRE team, estimate: 4)
AI-5: Run a safety canary for future ingress header changes that includes synthetic quota-bound traffic (owner: Platform QA, estimate: 2)
AI-6: Update runbook with step-by-step for pausing reconciliation and safe rollback checklist (owner: On-call SRE, estimate: 1)
